project.name: FoodSpots
project.purpose: Food spot discovery, reviews, and social recommendations — web only for now
project.ui_goal: Clean, functional desktop UI for testing. Mobile responsiveness is low priority.

tech_stack.frontend: React + Tailwind CSS + React Router v6
tech_stack.maps: MapLibre GL JS + MapTiler Cloud tiles (basemap, markers, heatmap layer) on the client; Google Directions API server-side for crawl routing

pages.name: Map View
pages.layout: Full-width map (70%) + right panel (30%) showing spot list
features: Click pin to preview spot in right panel

pages.name: Search & Discovery
pages.layout: Search bar top + filter sidebar (left) + results grid
pages.search_scope: Searches both dish names and spot names

pages.name: Spot Detail
pages.layout: Hero photo + info column (left 60%) + map mini + actions (right 40%)
sections: SpotHeader: name, cuisine tags, price range, open/closed badge, overall rating
QuickActions: Get Directions button, Save to List button, Share button
Dishes tab: dish cards with name, photo, avg dish rating
Reviews tab: review cards with author, rating, verified badge, photos, helpful votes
Owner Response: shown below review if owner replied

pages.name: Write Review
fields: Dish ratings (optional — pick dishes from spot's dish list, rate each)
Verified visit: auto GPS check, show green badge if within 100m of spot

pages.name: Food Crawl Planner
pages.layout: Left panel: spot picker + ordered list. Right panel: route drawn on a MapTiler map
features: Search and add spots to crawl
Live ETA and distance update via Google Directions API (waypoints)

pages.name: Curated Lists
pages.layout: Grid of list cards + Create List button top-right
features: Add spots to a list from Spot Detail page
View list: shows all spots in that list as cards

pages.name: Social Feed
pages.layout: Two-column: activity feed (left) + suggested users to follow (right)

pages.name: Leaderboard
pages.layout: Full-width ranked table + badge legend below

pages.name: Register
pages.layout: Centered card + onboarding step: pick cuisine preferences

shared_components: Navbar (top): Logo, Search bar, Notifications bell, User avatar menu
Sidebar (left): Home, Map, Search, Crawl, Lists, Social, Leaderboard
SpotCard: photo, name, cuisine, rating, price range, distance
ReviewCard: avatar, name, verified badge, star rating, text, photos, helpful buttons
DishCard: dish photo, name, avg rating
ListCard: cover photo, title, spot count, author

feature_logic.verified_visit: On review submit, compare user's submitted GPS coords with spot lat/lng. If distance < 100m, set verified_visit = true and award +1 bonus point.
feature_logic.trending: Spots sorted by review count in last 7 days DESC.
feature_logic.heatmap: Pass all spot lat/lng coordinates as a GeoJSON source to a MapLibre heatmap layer, heatmap-weight = review_count (normalised against the busiest spot in view).
feature_logic.food_crawl: Use Google Directions API with mode=driving and waypoints[] to compute route, total distance, and ETA.

ui_design.layout: Fixed left sidebar (220px) + top navbar (60px) + scrollable main content
ui_design.map_style: MapTiler 'streets-v2' style JSON so pins and heatmap stand out
ui_design.component_style: Rounded cards (radius 12px), subtle shadow, no heavy borders

deviations: Map tile rendering, markers and the heatmap use MapLibre GL JS against MapTiler Cloud (VITE_MAPTILER_KEY) instead of the Google Maps JavaScript API. Rationale: no Google Maps JS billing/loader on the client, and MapLibre ships a native heatmap layer.

The crawl route is still computed by the Google Directions API on the server (GOOGLE_MAPS_SERVER_KEY); the client only decodes the returned overview polyline and draws it as a MapLibre line layer. Stop ordering is unchanged — the user's drag order is sent as-is.
android_note: Android / React Native implementation is deferred. Backend API is built REST-first so it can be consumed by a mobile client later with zero changes. No mobile-specific logic in the backend.
